Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Education | National Rising school enrolment does not guarantee quality education – Edem Agbana Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 18 November 2026 11:57am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Member of Parliament for Ketu North, Edem Agbana, has cautioned that increasing school enrolment figures do not necessarily reflect improved access to quality education, warning that many children remain deprived of meaningful learning opportunities despite being in school.
He said the focus on expanding enrolment must be matched with efforts to address deeper challenges affecting the quality of education available to learners.
Speaking at the JoyNews-School for Life National Dialogue on Wednesday, November 18, Mr Agbana said access to education went beyond issues of gender, ethnicity and cultural background, stressing that the actual opportunities available to children within schools must also be considered.
Drawing on his experience, he noted that even in communities where children had access to schools, increasing enrolment did not automatically translate into better educational outcomes.
“Every time in terms of enrolment, you may have increased enrolment, but there is a deeper issue. The enrolment is not necessarily reflected in the kind of opportunities children have in schools,” he said.
He warned that growing enrolment figures could present an encouraging picture in official statistics without necessarily demonstrating that children were receiving quality education.
“We have a lot of children in schools, yet the numbers may be increasing and giving you some good picture of the statistics. By the end of the day, quality education is not being accessed by these children,” he added.
Mr Agbana also outlined Parliament's oversight mechanisms for monitoring the education sector, explaining that the Education Committee has an annual framework through which it invites various education agencies, including the Ghana Education Service (GES), to account for their performance.
He said the agencies brief the committee on their activities and progress, allowing members to identify shortcomings and make recommendations to address the gaps.
“For us as the Education Committee, we have a framework where every year we invite the various agencies in education, including the GES, for what we call performance audit. They brief us on what they are doing, where we identify gaps, and we make recommendations that those gaps should be closed,” he explained.
The MP stressed that assessing the education sector should not be limited to the number of children enrolled but should also examine whether learners are benefiting from meaningful educational opportunities.
